title: Reducing Reward Hacking by Localizing Bad Behavior Instead of Penalizing It
summary: Reducing Reward Hacking by Localizing Bad Behavior Instead of Penalizing It Alignment Science Blog Reducing Reward Hacking by Localizing Bad Behavior Instead of Penalizing It Shawn Hu¹*, Jake Ward¹* October 19, 2026 Aria Wong¹, Nathan Hu², Bryce Woodworth¹ Alexander Matt Turner³, Alex Cloud⁴ * Equal contribution; author order randomized ¹ MATS; ² Stanford; ³ FAR AI; ⁴ Anthropic tl;dr During training, models sometimes learn to cheat at tasks rather than solve them in the intended way, a problem known as reward hacking. One mitigation is to use an automated monitor to detect and penalize hacks, but this can teach the model to hack in ways the monitor can’t detect. We propose GRAFT, which instead confines the learning updates from detected hacks to a designated set of parameters that we remove after training. We find that removing these parameters can prevent reward hacks, including hacks that the monitors can’t detect. In our experiments, which are limited to small models and simple monitors, this method prevents reward hacks while still teaching the model to perform the intended task. 📄 Paper , 💻 Code This work was done as part of the MATS program. Background Reinforcement learning (RL) is an important component of frontier language model training. During RL, a model attempts to complete tasks given by a developer, and attempts are scored by a reward function. title: オープンエンドな探索を意思決定支援へ：推薦の質と多様性を高める「QD-Rec」を提案
summary: Sakana AIは、オープンエンドな探索の考え方を意思決定支援に応用した推薦手法「QD-Rec」を開発しました。QD-Recは、企業や顧客、論文などの「候補」と、それを選ぶ理由を述べた「仮説」の組を推薦の単位とし、過去の優れた仮説をもとに生成AIが新しい仮説を書くサイクルを繰り返します。これにより、質が高く切り口の異なる推薦を蓄積していきます。M&A、顧客ターゲティング、論文推薦の3つの課題で実験したところ、QD-Recは多くの設定で、毎回ゼロから仮説を書くベースラインなどより平均評価が高く、規模も大きい推薦の集合を構築しました。 論文： https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23470 技術記事： https://pub.sakana.ai/qd-rec/ コード： https://github.com/SakanaAI/QD-Rec はじめに どの企業を買収候補として検討するか。どの顧客に新しい製品を提案するか。膨大な論文の中から、次に何を読むか。こうした「多くの選択肢から一つを選ぶ」判断は、実社会のあらゆる場面にあります。その判断を支えるために、これまでさまざまな推薦アルゴリズムが研究されてきました。しかし、とくに複数の可能性を比較しながら方針を決める場面では、最もスコアの高い候補を一つ選んだり、上位の候補をランキングとして提示したりするだけでは、十分でないことがあります。 現実の意思決定に必要なのは、「何を選ぶか」に加えて、「なぜそれを選ぶのか」「選んだ先にどのような可能性があるのか」という具体的な提案です。例えば企業買収では、企業名とスコアだけでなく、「その企業の技術を自社の製品に組み込むことで、どのような価値を生み出せるか」といった事業のシナリオが判断材料になります。論文推薦でも、単に研究テーマが近いと示すだけでなく、「その手法を自分の研究にどう応用できるか」まで示されれば、読む価値を判断しやすくなります。ここでは、候補を選ぶ理由や期待される可能性を述べた文章を「仮説」と呼びます。 さらに、提案には多様性も必要です。有望な買収候補がいくつ見つかっても、すべてが同じ戦略に基づく提案なら、検討できる方向性は限られます。技術力の獲得、新しい市場への参入、既存事業との相乗効果など、異なる観点からの提案を比較できれば、最終的な候補を絞り込むためのショートリストにも幅が生まれます。目指すのは、単に種類の違う候補を並べることではなく、それぞれに検討する価値があり、選ぶ理由にも意味のある違いがある提案の集合です。 もちろん、推薦の説明可能性や多様性を重視する研究は、これまでも行われてきました。 ただし、同じ候補にも異なる切り口の仮説が考えられるため、生成AIで候補ごとに一つの理由を書くだけでは、有望な提案を見逃す可能性があります。かといって、数千件、ときには1万件を超える候補それぞれについて、さまざまな仮説を生成し、その妥当性や有用性を評価し尽くすのは、コストの面で現実的ではありません。私たちは、このように限られた予算の中で「候補」と「仮説」の組を探索し、質が高く多様な推薦を見つける問題を、「オープンエンドな推薦」として捉えました。 そこで着目したのが、オープンエンドな探索の研究で発展してきた Quality-Diversity （QD） です。QDは、単一の最良解だけを探すのではなく、異なる特徴を持つ、高品質な解の集合を見つけることを目指します。一つの方向で高得点の提案ばかりを集めるのではなく、異なる方向の提案を残し、それぞれを磨

title: AI will not automate radiologists like you think
summary: We have been talking for years now about AI automating jobs. Radiology has been a prime target, with Geoff Hinton once claiming, “people should stop training radiologists now, it’s just completely obvious that within five years, deep learning is going to do better than radiologists”, which is funny since he said that in 2016. There is now more demand for radiologists than ever, so clearly things did not turn out the way many thought. Here I will make a prediction that while radiology will change in the coming decade, radiologists will not be automated away any time soon. I will use radiology as an example but I think these principles will broadly apply to any field where demand can be elastic and quality can scale with increased intelligence. First of all, we have seen in the short history of language models that there is a “jagged edge of intelligence”, where AI excels at verifiable tasks with a lot of data but is underwhelming on less common tasks. One thing most AI researchers underestimate about radiology is that it is actually extremely multi-task. There are at least a hundred conditions that can be diagnosed from x-rays alone, and thousands using CT and MRI. AI will first master common and easy-to-see conditions and it will not be as good as experts at less-common diseases just because there is less data for that. title: Parallel Language Models via Variational Decoding
summary: Autoregressive language models emit one token per forward pass. This causes high inference latency, in particular as models are scaled up for quality. In this paper, we introduce Parallel Language Models (PLMs), which generate mutually consistent tokens in one forward pass by routing dependencies through latent auxiliary variables. PLMs are trained using a variational bound that reduces to an autoregressive loss plus a parallel decoding loss. Empirically, PLMs are on a faster and better Pareto frontier than autoregressive and discrete diffusion baselines. Pretrained PLMs achieve near-autoregressive pretraining loss on model scales of 80M to 3B parameters, and speedup follows a power law in model size. When post-trained, our 1.3B model matches or exceeds an identically trained autoregressive model on math, coding, and instruction-following benchmarks, speeding up inference $2.3\text{-}5.7\times$. Together, we show that parallel generation can be trained from a single training objective at autoregressive quality. We will make our code available at https://github.com/mandt-lab/plm.

title: TokenGate: Adapting LLMs for Fast and Memory-Efficient Prefill with Learned Token Pruning
summary: Expert human readers process large inputs (e.g., code repositories and long documents) by skimming to closely read only what matters. On the other hand, language models process all input tokens through each model layer, resulting in significant processing costs for long-context inputs. We introduce TokenGate, a small, drop-in component that extends existing trained models to enable end-to-end learnable token pruning over long-context inputs for fast and memory-efficient prefill. To enable end-to-end learning despite the non-differentiable top-K operator for token pruning, we introduce token-gated attention, a mechanism inspired by Mixture-of-Experts that re-weights attention logits using token importance scores. Across diverse tasks, TokenGate achieves $1.4$-$11.3\times$ faster time-to-first token (TTFT) and $1.5$-$3.4\times$ lower peak memory at no accuracy degradation for prefill in transformers. Compared to the best-performing prior methods for token-pruning, TokenGate gives up to $6.4\times$ faster prefill and $2\times$ lower peak memory. TokenGate natively extends both standard transformers (e.g., Qwen3) and hybrid-attention models (e.g., Qwen3.5) with simple lightweight adaptation comparable to standard parameter-efficient fine-tuning. We make our code available at: https://github.com/tokengate-models/TokenGate.

title: Managing Biological Risks from General-Purpose AI Models under the EU AI Act
summary: Managing Biological Risks from General-Purpose AI Models under the EU AI Act | GovAI About Research Opportunities Team Analysis Alumni Updates Donate About Research Opportunities Team Analysis Alumni Updates Donate Managing Biological Risks from General-Purpose AI Models under the EU AI Act Providers of general-purpose AI (GPAI) models with systemic risk must assess and mitigate biological risks under the EU AI Act. The voluntary General-Purpose AI Code of Practice specifies how signatories can meet these obligations and informs the European Commission’s assessment of alternative compliance approaches adopted by non-signatories. However, existing requirements grant providers considerable discretion over how biological risks are evaluated, documented, and communicated to the EU AI Office (“Office”). This creates three challenges for effective oversight: Biological risk evaluations are difficult to compare across providers because methods, baselines, and reporting formats differ. Evaluations have largely focused on standard external deployment, while other contexts that may materially change a model’s biological risk profile – such as trusted access programs – receive less consistent attention. There is limited visibility into how providers monitor, escalate, and respond to emerging biological risk findings before and after deployment.
